authors: Norman O. Smith, Steve Kelemen, Bartholomew Nagy
title: Solubility of natural gases in aqueous salt solutions-II. Nitrogen in aqueous NaCl, CaCl2, Na2SO4 and MgSO4 at room temperatures and at pressures below 1000 psia
experimental_method: Pressure decline method (apparatus described in Duffy et al. 1961, paper I of the series); N2 compressibility factors from the International Critical Tables; water-pumped N2 of 99.6 percent purity; Fisher certified salts, Na2SO4 N.F. grade, sulphates dried at 110 C, NaCl and CaCl2 water content found negligible by chloride titration.
uncertainties_stated: None given for the data; text only says agreement with Wiebe et al. is 'satisfactory for the present purpose; and within the expectations of the pressure decline method'.
quality_remarks: Authors say water results agree satisfactorily with Wiebe et al. (1933) and Henry's law holds in the range studied; their solubility in 2.0 N NaCl at 1 atm (5.1e-6 mole fraction) is about twice Braun's (1900) extrapolated value 3.2e-6. Total pressures were not corrected for water vapour (negligible). Salt solutions' pressure basis not stated explicitly. Table 4 title says 1.5 N NaCl, block heading and text say 1.38 N. Paper gives no solution densities, no temperature scale and no stated uncertainties. Table 7 (invariant liquid compositions at 500 psia, mole percent) is estimated from the tables by the authors, not measured; not extracted.
